cards.text: Picture it, baker. Moses, Israel's leader, has been preaching to the whole nation, and he's still going. Now he and the elders of Israel tell the people, "Keep all the commandments I am giving you today."
Then he gets specific: on the very day they cross the Jordan, they set up large stones and coat them with plaster. Kind of like icing a sugar cookie so the letters show up.

cards.question: Moses wants those big stones coated with plaster so something can go on them. What?

answers.text: All the words of this law
The names of the twelve tribes
The story of the river crossing

cards.text: Once they've crossed, the plastered stones go up on Mount Ebal, just as Moses commands. And there they're to build an altar too, an altar of stones to the LORD their God.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to shape the stones for the altar on Mount Ebal with iron tools.

cards.text: Uncut stones only, and on that altar they offer burnt offerings to the LORD. So a cookie stamper would be USELESS on Mount Ebal, because shaping things is my WHOLE job, friend!

cards.question: Israel is also to sacrifice peace offerings on the altar on Mount Ebal and eat them there in the presence of the LORD. What else does Moses tell them to do?

cards.text: Then Moses comes back to those stones: write all the words of this law, and write them distinctly, no blurry stamps. Trust me, baker, I stamped blurry for YEARS, and nobody wants a blurry law.
Now Moses and the Levitical priests speak to all Israel. A WHOLE nation in one crowd, and I've heard less noise from a mixer on high.

cards.question: What's the first thing Moses and the Levitical priests tell all Israel to do?
Moses and the priests tell Israel that this day they have become the ___ of the LORD their God.
Because Israel is now the LORD's people, Moses and the priests say they shall obey His voice and follow His commandments.

cards.text: That same day, Moses gives the tribes their spots for after the crossing. Six tribes stand on Mount Gerizim: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

cards.question: What are the six tribes on Mount Gerizim there to do?

cards.text: The other six stand on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali. Twelve tribes on two mountains, six and six, and somebody put REAL thought into this seating chart.

cards.question: The six tribes on Mount Ebal stand there to deliver the curse.

cards.text: Then the Levites get the loud part: they're to proclaim to every Israelite in a loud voice. My cookie cutter kid Ruby, the bell, would've LOVED this job.
First up: cursed is the man who makes a carved idol or molten image and sets it up in secret.

cards.question: After the Levites call out the curse on the secret idol, what are all the people to say?

cards.text: And the people are to say it after every single curse, twelve curses and twelve Amens. A whole nation told to agree out loud, and I can't get my ovens to agree on ONE temperature.

cards.question: The next curse comes home, to a man's own father or mother. What is he cursed for?
Then the Levites go to the edge of a neighbor's land: cursed is he who ___ his neighbor's boundary stone.
The next curse is about a blind man. What does the cursed person do to him?

answers.text: Lets him wander in the road

cards.question: Then three more people get named: cursed is he who withholds ___ from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow.

cards.text: Next, cursed is he who sleeps with his father's wife, for he has violated his father's marriage bed. And cursed is he who lies with any animal.
Cursed is he who sleeps with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother. And cursed is he who sleeps with his mother-in-law.

cards.question: The next curse is on the man who strikes down his neighbor in secret.

cards.text: Then, cursed is he who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person. I think that one lands heavy, friend.

cards.question: The last curse is only on the priests who don't put the words of this law into practice.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave those two mountains for now. Stick around, friend, this sermon's not done.
